# Five-minute website walkthrough

Format: real browser operation recording with English on-screen captions and AI-generated English narration. Total target: 5:00. The recording uses the local design preview.

## 0:00 — 01 / THE QUESTION

Which buildings warrant energy investigation—and which records need data review first?

## 0:14 — 01 / THE QUESTION

This explorer supports Boston energy planners, building managers and community sustainability organizations.

## 0:30 — 02 / EXPLORE

Start with building use and a reported ZIP area. Map colors compare energy per square foot with similar buildings.

## 0:45 — 02 / EXPLORE

Blue: more than 10% lower. Amber: more than 10% higher. Gray-blue: within 10% of the comparison level.

## 1:00 — 02 / EXPLORE

The map uses real Massachusetts ZIP boundaries. It represents Boston disclosure records, not all buildings in the state.

## 1:15 — 02 / EXPLORE

ZIP 02127 has 141 reported Multifamily buildings and 138 with valid comparisons. Its typical relative use is 7% higher.

## 1:30 — 03 / COMPARE

Search for BERDO 100083: 21–23 Beacon Street. Compare its energy intensity with buildings of similar use and size.

## 1:45 — 03 / COMPARE

This building uses 93.6 kBtu per square foot per year. Its comparison-group median is 53.4: about 75% higher.

## 2:00 — 03 / COMPARE

The reference contains 159 eligible Multifamily buildings in the 100,000–249,999 square-foot size band.

## 2:15 — 03 / COMPARE

Benchmarks stay fixed when filters change. High energy intensity is a reason to investigate, not proof of poor management.

## 2:30 — 03 / COMPARE

First recommendation: verify operating hours, occupancy and metering before choosing an energy audit or retrofit study.

## 2:45 — 04 / SCENARIO

The scenario asks what happens if a building moves partway toward its similar-building median.

## 3:00 — 04 / SCENARIO

At 0%, no change is applied. Missing or ineligible data is excluded rather than treated as zero.

## 3:15 — 04 / SCENARIO

At 50%, this example moves halfway toward typical use: a 2.65 million kBtu difference, or 21% of reported energy.

## 3:30 — 04 / SCENARIO

At 100%, the full above-median gap is closed: 5.30 million kBtu. This is an illustration, not verified engineering savings.

## 3:45 — 04 / SCENARIO

The same calculation can apply to the current map selection. Buildings already below their median stay unchanged.

## 4:00 — 05 / EVIDENCE

The full analysis includes distributions, an interactive scatterplot, and a searchable table with coordinated filters and CSV export.

## 4:15 — 05 / EVIDENCE

Second recommendation: review invalid inputs first. BERDO 102879 has negative energy values and must not enter an energy scenario.

## 4:30 — 05 / LIMITATIONS

Campus summaries and member buildings are kept separate. A single disclosure cannot establish trends, policy effects or achievable savings.

## 4:45 — 05 / LIMITATIONS

Data, methodology and reflection are available in Data & methods. The release is labeled 2025; the energy-use year remains unconfirmed.
